observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: Three views at one scale of an olive-brown armoured body piled in three tiers, with overlapping plates and one hooked spine under each plate. South is a broad dome with a face and a large clawed lobe at each lower corner. East is the longest view: a coil with the head at upper right and one clawed lobe at lower left. North is visibly narrower, a tapered stepped pyramid with a small cap on top and one clawed lobe at bottom centre. All sit on clean transparency.

Front view, almost perfectly mirror-symmetric. A wrinkled pink-brown fleshy face with small hooded dark eyes and a downturned mouth sits under a wide shield plate on the top tier, with two curved hooks beside the mouth. Below it are two wider tiers of rounded plates with hooked spines. Two heavy clawed lobes splay out at the bottom left and right of the lowest tier. The shading is smooth and slightly sculpted.

True side profile of a long segmented body coiled in three tiers. The head is at the right end of the top tier, with a shield plate, a small eye, a wrinkled snout and downward hooks. Spines run along each tier's lower edge. A single clawed lobe trails from the lower left, and the right end of the bottom tier is smooth with no limb. This view is slightly darker and more olive, with a more painterly texture than south and north.

Rear view with no face or eyes. Three plated tiers narrow sharply upward to a small ridged cap. A single fleshy tapering lobe with three claws runs down the centre of the lowest tier toward the camera. The silhouette is a pyramid rather than a dome. Measured at alpha above 32, it is 330 px wide with 59023 opaque px, against south at 420 px and 84798 px.

A vanilla human beside the east view on a brown ground, with the grid drawn at 211 px per cell. The candidate measures about 191 by 119 px, so about 0.9 cell wide and 0.56 cell tall, well below the human's head height. In the normal-play inset it is a small dark banded mound next to a human and a rat, and the head cannot be picked out.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows plated back tiers and a clawed rear lobe, with no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three views stand on a ground line at the game's angled camera; none is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured height spread of 3% is fine, but at that height north is only 330 px wide against south's 420 px, with about 70% of south's opaque area. North looks like the smaller animal in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: South has two large clawed lobes at the lower corners. East has one, at the rear lower left, and nothing at the front end. North has one, at bottom centre. The structure does not turn with the body.

SIGNATURE.seen: The dormant coil of a long body is clear on east. South and north read as a stacked dome, so 'long, low' is legible on east only (see finding).

ALIEN.seen: Three stacked plated coils with a hooked spine under each plate and clawed lobes are no Earth animal. South's shell dome and wrinkled face do lean toward a tortoise (see finding). The card lists no departures to check.

STYLE.seen: Painterly plate texture, muted natural colour, dull eyes and no cel shading or heavy keyline; south and north are a little smoother than east.

OURS.seen: An invented armoured coil body drawn for this subject, with no vanilla or other-mod animal recognisable.

ALPHA.seen: Clean edges on the checkerboard, with no ground patch, shadow, rock or halo under the body.

SCALE.seen: The panel shows about 0.9 cell wide (191 px at 211 px per cell), which would fit 'low'. drawSize 2.7 implies about 2.45 cells wide and 1.5 tall (465/512 and 293/512 of 2.7), taller than the human. Missing: a panel that demonstrably renders at the stated drawSize.

reply.subject: RSW_TunnelSnake
reply.image_seen: Image 1 compares three brown armored, tiered coils; image 2 shows a frontal wrinkled face and two lateral clawed lobes; image 3 shows a right-facing head and one rear clawed lobe; image 4 shows a narrower rear stack and central clawed projection without eyes; image 5 shows the creature squat and broad beside a taller human, with a normal-play inset.

concerns.evidence: South has two substantial clawed projections at opposite lower corners. East shows one at the rear, while north shows a single central projection connected to the rear body. These views do not establish a consistent arrangement of appendages or a single continuous tail.

On the shared-scale panel, north has a visibly narrower lower coil and more sharply tapering upper tiers than south. The supplied width and opaque-area measurements support this remaining bulk discrepancy. The measured 3% height spread itself is acceptable.

Tortoise is the nearest shell-like association, but the pictures show three distinct tiers of overlapping armor around a coiled body, with an elongated head emerging from the upper tier in east. That overall construction reads as an armored alien coil rather than a recognizable tortoise with added decorations.

South forms a high, three-tier dome and north a steeply tapered stack. East reveals some length, but retains the same raised stack. Coiling fits the description, yet the stacked presentation obscures the defining low, corridor-hugging serpentine body.

The frontal mouth is downturned, but its irregular folds, small recessed eyes and heavy armored brow read as fleshy predator anatomy. There are no glossy oversized eyes, simplified smile or flat cartoon shading.

All three views share mottled brown-olive plates, ochre edge wear, dark seams and wrinkled exposed flesh. South and north are more symmetric compositions, but their visible surface treatment does not establish a different rendering style from east.

The scale panel provides a usable comparison: the coiled creature is substantially shorter than the human and occupies a broad ground footprint. The description specifies no human-relative size that this contradicts. Its tall coil proportions are addressed separately in K4.

findings.seen: South shows two lateral clawed lobes, east one rear lobe, and north one central clawed projection; their number and attachment do not resolve into the same anatomy across views.
findings.quote: Every structure (horns, fans, sails, tails) is present and turns with the body in every view
findings.fix: All three facings show the same continuous armored body and clearly identifiable tail or appendages, with matching count, attachment and placement as the creature turns.

findings.seen: North retains a substantially narrower, more tapered coil mass than the broad south dome despite their matched heights.

findings.fix: The north view carries the same substantial lower-coil volume and overall body mass as the south view at the shared scale.

The body is one continuous plated limbless serpent with a single head end and a single tail end; the armoured plates, the flank spur ridge and the tail paddle keep the same count, attachment and placement as the creature turns.

The rear view carries the full lower-coil volume of the front view, so its outline is a wide rounded mound with a broad base.

limbless body of broad overlapping carapace plates with a ridge of short gripping spurs along each flank

request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the yanker, an invented alien corridor predator. A long, low ambush hunter built for a tunnel: it lies dormant in a flat, sprawling coil, two low overlapping loops spread side by side, wedged into one narrow gap, and it wakes only when prey comes within touching distance. The coil is a broad flat mound about 340 px wide and about 150 px tall, roughly 2.3 times wider than tall, with a wide base and a gently rounded crown. Its width, thickness and bulk are identical in every facing. The plated segments wrap visibly around the pile and run on into one another, so a single long, low, continuous serpentine body is legible. Anatomy: a heavy blunt wedge of a head with a wide hinged mouth ringed by thick pouchy lip-flaps and short hooked grasping palps at the jaw corners, small recessed eyes under bony brow ridges. The head is held close to the ground, resting low on the front edge of the coil with the jaw near the floor line. The long limbless body is built from broad overlapping armoured plates like a segmented carapace, dark mottled leathery hide with pale rubbery seams and a velvety sheen, and a ridge of short gripping spurs along each flank that brace against corridor walls. One continuous body with exactly one head end and one tail end. The tail ends in a single thick blunt anchoring paddle with a cluster of hooked grip-spurs, trailing from the lower rear of the coil. Colour: deep olive-brown hide, pale rubbery seams, darker plates. Front view (south), eyes toward the viewer: the low head rests at the front of the broad flat coil, and the tail paddle is tucked behind the coil with only its tip showing at lower centre. Side view (east), profile: the low head at the front of the coil with the spur ridge visible along the flank, and the single tail paddle trailing from the rear lower left. Rear view (north), seen from behind: the plated back and spur ridge face the viewer in the same broad flat mound, with the same width at every tier and the same rounded outline as the front view; the head is hidden behind the coil and the single tail paddle sits centred at the bottom of the coil, toward the viewer. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, clean dark outline with soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.

observed.facings.png: Three views at one scale on a checkerboard, with no ground or halo. South is a head-on crouching animal with a wide rounded body. East is a long, low, hunched rodent in true profile. North is the rear, with rounded haunches, a tail curled against one side and two ears above the back. All three share the same scruffy brown-tan fur over pinkish wrinkled skin. South and north look plumper than the lean east body.
observed.south.png: Front view with the face toward the camera: long snout seen head-on, small dark nose, slightly open mouth, small narrowed dull reddish eyes, and a pale wispy chin tuft. Tall pink-lined ears have tufted tips. Thin stringy fur lies over pinkish-grey skin. Two forelegs and two hind feet end in dark long-toed clawed paws. A ringed tail shows curving along the image-left flank. The body is broad and nearly ball-shaped.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right, with an arched back and long narrow head. Patchy tan fur has darker mottling along the back and bare wrinkled pink skin on the flank. It has small teeth, a pale chin tuft, a tall ear plus the far ear, and a small dull reddish eye. Three feet are visible, all dark and long-clawed. The pale ringed tail leaves the rump and curls tightly down against the haunch, ending behind the hind knee. It is fairly thick and roughly a third of the body length.
observed.north.png: Rear view with no face or eyes: haunches, shaggy mottled back and two ears above. The ears show their pink inner surface even though they are seen from behind. The ringed tail curls down across the image-left haunch. Two hind feet with dark claws are visible. The shape is rotund and wider at the bottom.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom beside the human it is about one cell long, a little shorter than the human is tall, low-slung and wider than the human. At 32 px per cell it is a soft pale tan shape on a similar tan ground. The ear and quadruped outline can be made out, but it looks faint beside the black-outlined human and vanilla rat, and its body is only a little bigger than the rat's.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on with eyes, nose, mouth and chin tuft toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows haunches, back and tail, with no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: No facing is a dorsal view. South and north stand on their feet at the game camera angle, and east is a profile.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The card prints a 1% height spread, and the panel shows matching ground line and ear height.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Fur, skin, ears, ringed tail and paws carry across all three views, and the style now agrees across facings. Small mismatches are reported as polish findings.

SIGNATURE.seen: A large scruffy rodent reads at once on every facing, and the east view shows the predator's teeth and claws.

ALIEN.seen: It reads as a giant mangy rat, which is what the card asks for: earth_body_named is yes and the canon specifies a rat-like body. No departures are listed. The wrinkled bare skin, tufted ears and chin tuft keep it from being an ordinary rat.

CANON.seen: Every line holds except part of BODY PLAN: the tail is curled tight to the haunch, fairly thick, and roughly a third of body length rather than as long as the body.

STYLE.seen: Soft painted realism with fine hair and wrinkled skin. It has no ink keyline, no glossy eyes and no smile, and it does not read as a photo or 3D render.

OURS.seen: The provenance is this project's own redraw batch, and the picture is not the vanilla rat shown in the scale panel.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha is measured on all facings. On the checkerboard and on a ground-colour test there is no halo, ground patch or shadow.

SCALE.seen: It is wider than the human and about one cell long, which fits 'large' and bigger than a big dog. The 2 m canon size is less clear: see the polish finding and proposal.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it is a soft shape close in value to the tan ground, with no dark edge, and the tail merges into the body. The rat outline can be made out but is not a few bold shapes.

request.subject: RSW_WompRat

edits.change: The tail is very long and thin, naked and pale grey with darker rings along its length. It is as long as the body from rump to nose. It leaves the centre of the rump and trails out behind the body in a long, gently curving taper.

The tail is visible on every facing. In the side view it trails fully behind the rump in a graceful S-curve, clearly showing its length and rings. In the front view its pale ringed tip appears past the animal's right hip. In the rear view it runs back from the rump and its length is readable. The tail is a slender pale-grey cord, much thinner than the hind leg and visibly different in colour from the brown fur.

The tail always sweeps toward the animal's own right flank. In the front view, with eyes toward the viewer, that is the image-left side. In the rear view, seen from behind, the same flank is the image-right side. In the side view the tail trails straight back, with its tip curving slightly toward the viewer-facing side.
The sprite keeps a wide margin of empty canvas on every side. The body is drawn somewhat smaller so that the full-length tail also sits inside the canvas. Body bulk stays the same in every facing.

invariants: Palette and fur colouring of the body, identical to the previous render
Large, heavy-bodied rodent with a thick broad torso and a predator-scavenger's teeth
Body scale, shoulder and haunch width, and ear and paw size are the same in every facing
The rear view shows back, tail and haunches, with eyes hidden
Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld style, clean dark outline, transparent background, exactly one creature, centred
request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the womp rat. Womp rats were large, omnivorous rodents native to Tatooine that were widely considered to be pests. While womp rats were opportunists and fond of carrion, they were also predators. Visible features it must show: the canon Tatooine womp rat (see canon entry womprat); a large, heavy-bodied rodent with a thick broad torso; a predator-scavenger's teeth; and a very long, thin, naked, pale-grey tail with darker rings along its length. The tail is as long as the body from rump to nose. It is a slender cord much thinner than the hind leg, and it leaves the centre of the rump and trails out behind the body in a long, gently curving taper. Body scale is identical in every facing: the front view's broad shoulders and chest, the side view's substantial rump, and the rear view's wide hunched haunches, thick rump and substantial dark paws planted wide all carry equal bulk, fill the same width at the same height, and show ears and paws of the same size. The tail appears on every facing and always sweeps toward the animal's own right flank. In the side view the tail trails fully behind the rump in a graceful S-curve, so its whole length and rings are readable. In the front view, with eyes toward the viewer, the pale ringed tail tip appears past the animal's right hip, on the image-left side. The rear view is seen from behind, showing back, tail and haunches, with eyes hidden; its haunches are as wide as the front view's shoulders and chest, and the pale ringed tail runs back from the centre of the rump and sweeps toward the animal's right flank, which is the image-right side in this view. The creature is drawn with a wide margin of empty canvas on every side, with the body somewhat smaller in the frame so the whole body and the full-length tail sit inside the canvas at the same scale in every facing. Keep the palette, fur colouring and body plan identical to the previous render. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, soft painted edges in a deeper shade of the local colour, clean dark outline. Exactly ONE creature, centred, the whole body and tail visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.

reply.subject: RM_Qorrax

observed.facings.png: Three views at one scale on a checkerboard, all the same height. A crimson, wet-skinned cephalopod body is held clear of the ground on arching tentacles with pale sucker rims. South and north are compact domes with tentacles splayed either side. East is a long spindle-shaped body with a hook-beaked head at the right.
observed.south.png: Head-on front view. A ridged, domed mantle sits above a low face with two small amber eyes under heavy brows and a grey-black hooked beak pointing down, closed. About ten tentacles fan out and down, including two short inner ones behind. Nothing is under the body.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. A long mantle tapers to a point at the left and has faint raised ridges under the skin. The head runs forward like a raptor's, with a ringed eye and an open, hooked, dark beak. About nine tentacles arch down from the belly to the ground in a staggered, stride-like arrangement, with the far ones darker. The body is lifted well above the tips.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The back of the mantle shows a central ridge with ribbing either side, narrowing to a small point low down at the centre. There are no eyes, face or beak. Tentacles splay out and down as on south, with sucker rims visible on the outer ones.
observed.scale.png: Human on the left, candidate on the right, on tan ground with a cell grid. At max zoom the candidate is about 161 px long at 211 px per cell, roughly 0.76 cells, and well under half the human's height. In the normal-play inset it is about 25 px long, shorter than the rat beside it, and is a small red smear with thin legs.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the front: face toward the camera, both eyes visible, beak head-on at the centre.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the rear: back of the mantle with a dorsal ridge and rear point, no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: No facing is overhead. South and north are seen from the front and rear at the game angle, with tentacles falling downward rather than radiating all round, and east is a side profile.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The card measures a 0% height spread. Mantle height also looks matched across views. The audit's complaint is gone: at the widest span in the top 45% of the body, north is 148 px and south is 162 px, so north no longer reads bulkier.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same animal throughout: crimson wet skin, pale sucker rims, dark hooked beak and ridged mantle, all turned with the body. Small differences are reported as a polish finding.

SIGNATURE.seen: Running on tentacles and the hooked beak both read at a glance. The internal shell shows only as faint ridges under unbroken skin, which suits an internal shell.

ALIEN.seen: The front and rear views read as an octopus and the tapered east mantle as a squid, which the description allows because it names a squid body. The tentacle stance and raptor-like head take it well away from a plain cephalopod.

DEPARTURES.seen: Line 1, stands and runs on its tentacles as legs instead of trailing them: present. On east the body is lifted clear and the tentacles arch down to the ground in a staggered stride. South and north also show the body held up on them.

STYLE.seen: Painterly and realistic, with mottled skin and wet highlights. The eyes are small and hard under heavy brows, so it is not cute. The strong gloss leans slightly toward a digital sculpt but does not read as a 3D render or a photo.

OURS.seen: The card's provenance is our own redraw batch, and nothing resembles a vanilla or borrowed sprite.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on the checkerboard with no backdrop, ground, water or shadow. Alpha histogram: body pixels are mostly 253, not 255, and there are 825 to 2639 near-invisible pixels of alpha 1 to 7 per facing. Neither is visible.

SCALE.seen: scale.png does not show the adult size on the card. The candidate spans about 0.76 cells, which matches a 0.8-cell draw (491/512 x 0.8 = 0.77), while the card's drawSize of 3.8 predicts about 3.64 cells. Missing: a panel drawn at drawSize 3.8. See the SCALE_WRONG finding for what the art does at that size.

LEGIBLE.seen: Judged from my own render of east at drawSize 3.8 and 32 px per cell, because the supplied inset is too small. The red body, legs and dark beak read as bold shapes against tan ground, though the pale tentacle tips fade somewhat. In the supplied inset, at about 25 px long, it is only a small red smear.

reply.subject: RM_Qorrax
reply.image_seen: The montage shows three red, fleshy tentacle-walker facings; south has paired eyes and a central beak, east has an elongated pointed mantle and hooked beak, north shows an eyeless rear mantle, and the scale panel shows the low-bodied creature beside a human.

concerns.evidence: East exposes the hooked beak's curved opening in profile; south shows its central dark cleft head-on. Both are compatible with the same beak. North shows the pointed rear mantle end-on, with more of its upper surface visible; its lower projected tip does not establish a different attachment. Tentacles overlap and obscure their roots in every facing, so differing visible tip counts do not demonstrate different anatomy. The red mantle, pale underside and supporting tentacles remain consistent.

The scale panel shows a horizontally elongated animal with a substantial mantle and a broad spread of supporting tentacles. Its height is well below the human's, but that follows its low squid-derived body plan; the visible overall dimensions are compatible with a deer-sized animal. At normal play scale, the pointed mantle and tentacle-supported silhouette remain distinguishable.
